memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its accessories, and the olive oil for the light; the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent; the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand; the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases, and the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard; the ropes and tent pegs for the courtyard; all the furnishings for the tabernacle, the tent of meeting." - Exod 39:37-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The list keeps going. Lampstand, oil, altar, incense, basin, curtains, ropes, tent pegs. It ends with the smallest items on the whole inventory.

Ropes and tent pegs, listed alongside the golden lampstand. Both brought. Both counted. Both necessary.

Scripture could have summarised: "and everything else." It does not. It names them.

That tells us something about how God sees the contributions of His people. In a world that celebrates the visible and forgets the rest, God keeps a full inventory. He is not unjust; He will not forget your work and the love you have shown Him as you have helped His people (Heb 6:10).

The one who prayed faithfully for decades is on the list. The one who gave quietly. The one who kept a home warm so others could serve. The one who did the unglamorous job nobody applauded.

Nothing was left behind in the workshop. Nothing was considered too minor to bring.

Whatever you have done for God — however small it looked, however unnoticed it went — it is not lost. It is on the list.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What faithful service of yours has felt unnoticed?
2. Do you value in others what God values, or only what is visible?
3. Whose "ropes and tent pegs" work could you thank this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that nothing done for You is forgotten. Help me serve faithfully whether or not it is seen. Amen.
